titulo: The last morning, before the bag is out of your hands
subtitulo: Check out, leave the luggage safely, tip the person who actually cleaned the room, and close on a real goodbye
cena: The lobby is full of other people's suitcases, and yours is about to join the pile for six more hours before the flight — if you say the right sentence first.
frasePiso: The trip does not end at checkout. It ends when the bag is stored, the last person is thanked, and you leave the way you arrived.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Standard hotel checkout in Mexico is typically around midday (commonly 12:00–13:00), with late checkout available for an additional charge depending on the hotel's own policy and the hour requested.
fatosDatados.fonte: Práticas hoteleiras convergentes reportadas por guias de viagem (Villa Experience, Frommer's, Mexperience); confirmar política do estabelecimento específico

fatosDatados.afirmacao: A common practice for tipping housekeeping in Mexico is 25–50 pesos per day, left visibly in the room, since the person cleaning may change daily.
fatosDatados.fonte: Guias de viagem convergentes sobre gorjeta em hotéis mexicanos (Villa Experience, Afar, The Real Deal Tours)

steps.pt: Last morning. Close the room, store the bag properly, thank the people who made it work — leave with a sentence, not silence.

steps.es: Buenos días. ¿Todo bien con la habitación?
steps.pt: Good morning. Everything all right with the room?
steps.tts: Buenos días. ¿Todo bien con la habitación?

steps.promptPt: Reception asks how the room was. Confirm and say you're here to check out. Speak now.
steps.es: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.
steps.pinyin: TOH-doh byen, GRAH-syahs. BEN-goh ah AH-sehr el chek-OWT
steps.pt: All good, thanks. I'm here to check out.
steps.tts: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.

steps.pt: Of course. One moment, please.
Flight's late tonight, checkout clock doesn't care — don't carry the bag all day, ask the one question that solves it.

steps.es: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh deh-HAR mee mah-LEH-tah ah-KEE AHS-tah lah TAR-deh
steps.pt: Can I leave my suitcase here until the afternoon?
steps.tts: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?

steps.promptPt: Your flight isn't until tonight. Ask whether you can leave your suitcase here until the afternoon. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh deh-HAR mee mah-LEH-tah ah-KEE AHS-tah lah TAR-deh
steps.pt: Can I leave my suitcase here until the afternoon?

steps.es: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.
steps.pt: Yes, of course. Here's your claim ticket.
steps.tts: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.

steps.pt: Hold onto that comprobante — same logic as B14 and B15's receipts, the paper that gets your bag back without argument.

steps.es: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?
steps.pt: Would you like to leave a tip for the housekeeper?
steps.tts: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?

steps.pt: Genuinely voluntary, unlike B14's automatic line — commonly a small daily amount left visibly, but the choice is yours.

steps.es: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.
steps.pinyin: see, yah lah deh-HEH en lah ah-bee-tah-SYOHN
steps.pt: Yes, I already left it in the room.
steps.tts: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.

steps.promptPt: You already left a tip in the room this morning. Confirm that. Speak now.
steps.es: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.
steps.pinyin: see, yah lah deh-HEH en lah ah-bee-tah-SYOHN
steps.pt: Yes, I already left it in the room.
Last piece, one sentence — not a review, just the same close you used all module: thanks, and see you.

steps.es: Gracias por su visita. Que tenga buen viaje.
steps.pt: Thank you for your visit. Have a good trip.
steps.tts: Gracias por su visita. Que tenga buen viaje.

steps.promptPt: Close the stay the way you closed every counter this trip. Thank them and say goodbye. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much. See you.

steps.encaixe: usar el baño antes de irme
steps.promptPt: Checked out, bag stored, long ride ahead. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Puedo usar el baño antes de irme?
steps.pinyin: PWEH-doh oo-SAHR el BAH-nyoh AHN-tehs deh EER-meh
steps.pt: Can I use the bathroom before I go?
steps.tts: ¿Puedo usar el baño antes de irme?

steps.promptPt: You need it for expenses. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I have the invoice?

steps.promptPt: Ask the desk to do it for you. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you call me a taxi?

steps.promptPt: It is raining and the taxi is late. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I wait in here?

steps.es: Vengo a hacer el check-out. ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde? Muchas gracias. Hasta luego.
steps.pinyin: BEN-goh ah AH-sehr el chek-OWT. PWEH-doh deh-HAR mee mah-LEH-tah ah-KEE AHS-tah lah TAR-deh. MOO-chahs GRAH-syahs. AHS-tah LWEH-goh
steps.pt: Shadow the whole last morning, start to close.
steps.tts: Vengo a hacer el check-out. ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde? Muchas gracias. Hasta luego.

steps.pt: B18 complete, básico with it. Check out, claim ticket, tip on your terms, close with the same words you opened with.

aprofundar.titulo: The last hours are still part of the stay

secoes.titulo: Checkout time is the hotel's, not the flight's
secoes.corpo: Standard checkout runs mid-morning to early afternoon depending on the property, and a flight that leaves at night does not extend it automatically. Ask for storage rather than assuming you can keep the room key past the stated hour.

secoes.titulo: A claim ticket beats a memory
secoes.corpo: The same logic that made you ask for receipts in B14 and B15 applies to a stored bag: a physical comprobante is the artifact that gets it back without a debate.

secoes.titulo: The housekeeping tip is genuinely optional
secoes.corpo: Unlike the automatic restaurant charge B14 taught you to question, a tip for housekeeping in Mexico is a voluntary local custom, not a fee. A commonly reported range is 25–50 pesos per day, left visibly, but the decision belongs to the traveller.
Muchas gracias and hasta luego are the same two moves B02 opened the whole course with. The course ends where it began, on purpose.

permissao: You are allowed to ask for a storage claim ticket instead of just trusting a pile of bags behind a desk. That small piece of paper is not you being difficult with people who have been kind to you all week — it's the one artifact that makes the system work for everyone.
espelho: Anyone who has ever left a hotel gym bag with the front desk and asked for a numbered tag back home already trusts this exact system — a comprobante is just that same instinct, applied on the last day in a language that isn't yours yet.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Reception asks if you'd like to leave a tip for housekeeping, and you're not sure whether it's expected, how much, or whether you've already missed the moment.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I should have handled this earlier, or there's a fixed amount I'm supposed to know.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Unlike the restaurant tip line in B14, which can appear on a bill without your consent, a housekeeping tip in Mexico is a voluntary custom with no fixed national amount — commonly a small sum left daily, since the person cleaning may change from day to day.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: If you haven't already, you can still leave it in the room or hand it over at the desk; there's no single correct moment, and 'ya la dejé' is a perfectly normal answer if you already did.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You close the stay without anxiety about a custom that was always flexible, not a test you could fail.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a reason to assume every hotel charge is optional — this specifically applies to the housekeeping tip, not to charges the hotel states as mandatory, like some late-checkout fees.
